Evil Dead Burn Review — This One Hits Different (And Not How You Think)

short // Jul 12, 2026 · Updated Sep 24, 2026

Watch on YouTube

Evil Dead Burn is here, and it's a really fun movie. But these new Evil Dead movies are trying to tell us something, y'all: we can't have any family reunions. I feel like somebody was watching Madea's Family Reunion and said, "What if we add Evil Dead into the mix?"

Six movies in, Burn also made something impossible to ignore. There's no chosen one tying this franchise together anymore. Just survivors.

What Evil Dead Burn gets right

Let me give it its flowers first, because it earns them.

  • The action is intense, and it doesn't let up.
  • The gore goes hard, and the practical effects still land. There's more CGI in this one than in the last two, and you'll notice it, but when the real stuff shows up, it hits.
  • The Deadites are center stage, right where they belong.

That last one matters most. Just like the 2013 Evil Dead and Evil Dead Rise, Burn has some really great moments with the Deadites. That specific kind of wrong, something wearing the face of somebody you love and enjoying it, is fully intact. If there's one thing this new era gets right every single time, it's the Deadites.

If you came for a nasty night at the movies, you're getting one.

The chosen one problem

Here's what hit me on the way out.

This movie made something more noticeable than the other two did: there's no sense of a chosen one tying them together. Every entry in the new era runs the same shape. Ordinary people, one terrible night, somebody they love turns into something else, and whoever's left tries to make it to sunrise.

It works, and it's scary. But nobody carries you from one movie into the next, and six movies in, you feel that hole.

The return that let me down

Y'all probably already know that someone returns from the previous film. I won't spell it out for anybody who hasn't seen it yet, but I'll be honest: I was a bit disappointed.

And that's what made me realize how much this new series is missing the fan-favorite elements that made the original run so beloved.

What the old Evil Dead had that the new era doesn't

Remember when Evil Dead was this?

  • A Farewell to Arms. Ash cuts off his own possessed hand in Evil Dead II, traps it under a bucket and stacks books on top, with that one sitting right there.
  • Having a conversation with yourself in the mirror about what happened to your girlfriend.
  • Being that guy with the gun. This is my boomstick.
  • Having a bunch of mini-mes trying to take you out in Army of Darkness.

That was Evil Dead. Horror and slapstick at the same time, with one unforgettable guy in the middle of all of it.

Now it's mostly wolves in familiar clothing. "Mommy's with the maggots now." It's effective, and Rise is a great movie, but it's a completely different identity.

Bruce Campbell is in it (kind of)

Yes, Bruce Campbell is in Evil Dead Burn. He has a cameo as one of the photos on the wall, watching over the family like, "You got this, right?"

He is not playing Ash in this one, y'all. It's very confusing. Campbell has even shot down the fan theory that his photo is supposed to be the family's grandfather. Love it or hate it, that's classic Evil Dead for you.

How the leaks held up

Before release, I went through every alleged leak from the L.A. test screenings and sorted what looked real from the fan fiction. Now that the movie's out, most of the big ones landed, but not all of them. That article has the full scorecard.

Update (September 2026)

Here's how Burn did after this review went up:

  • Box office: It opened in fourth place with about $13.7 million and finished around $72.3 million worldwide, on a reported $20 million budget.
  • Reviews: It sits at about 71% on Rotten Tomatoes, where the critics' consensus calls it "the meanest, nastiest, and ickiest chapter." Audiences gave it a B CinemaScore.
  • Stay through the credits: Burn has two post-credits scenes. I break both of them down in the leaks article.
  • What's next: Evil Dead Wrath, from writer-director Francis Galluppi, is a prequel set in 1972, due in theaters April 7, 2028.

Sources: Wikipedia: Evil Dead Burn, Deadline on Evil Dead Wrath

Quick answers

Is Evil Dead Burn good? Yes. It's a fun, brutal horror movie with intense action, strong practical gore and great Deadites, even with more CGI than the last two films.

Is Bruce Campbell in Evil Dead Burn? Only as a cameo in a photo on the wall. He doesn't play Ash.

Is Ash in Evil Dead Burn? No. The new era follows ordinary families instead of a chosen-one hero like Ash Williams.

Does Evil Dead Burn have a post-credits scene? Yes, it has two, so stay through the credits.

What's the next Evil Dead movie? Evil Dead Wrath, a prequel set in 1972, due in theaters April 7, 2028.

Your turn

Do you miss the old series with Ash, or do you like the new Deadite experience? Tell me in the comments.
